T: Steal the bread, keep the silver, and check the innkeeper's bill twice.
D: In 19th-century France, a convict breaks his parole to start a new life, while a relentless police inspector spends years hunting him down.
P: Serve the bread when the Bishop of Digne sits Valjean down at his table and feeds him.
S: Valjean's loaf with salted butter and radishes
the one loaf of bread that cost him nineteen years

A crackling, dark-crusted country loaf torn at the table, with salted butter, crisp radishes and salt flakes. Mix 500g bread flour, 7g dried yeast, 10g salt and 400ml warm water to a sticky dough and cover for 2 hours until doubled. Tip onto a floured bench, fold the edges in to make a round and set seam side down on floured baking paper. Heat the oven to 240C with a lidded cast iron pot inside for 30 minutes. Lift the loaf on its paper into the pot, slash the top and bake for 25 minutes with the lid on, then 15 minutes with it off, until dark and crusty. Cool for 30 minutes, then tear and serve with 125g soft salted butter, a bunch of trimmed radishes and salt flakes.
the Thénardiers' inn at Montfermeil, where every bill comes padded

Pork belly slow-cooked with garlic and thyme until it falls apart, shredded into its own fat, with toasted baguette, cornichons and mustard. Heat the oven to 150C. Toss 800g cubed pork belly with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper in a small lidded casserole with 4 garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves, 4 thyme sprigs and 200ml water. Cover and cook for 3 hours until the meat falls apart. Pick out the herbs, shred the pork and garlic with two forks and work in enough of the fat to make it soft. Pack into jars, pour the rest of the fat over and chill for 2 hours until set. Serve at room temperature with toasted baguette, cornichons and Dijon mustard.
M: Monsieur Thénardier carving at the head of the table while he picks his guests' pockets

Chicken thighs braised in red wine with smoky bacon, eschalots, mushrooms and thyme, with buttery boiled potatoes. Fry 150g smoked bacon lardons in a large casserole until crisp and lift out. Season 1.5kg bone-in chicken thighs and brown well in the fat, then lift out. Brown 12 peeled eschalots and 250g button mushrooms in the pot. Stir in 2 crushed garlic cloves and 2 tbsp plain flour, then 750ml red wine, 250ml chicken stock, 2 bay leaves and 4 thyme sprigs. Return the chicken and bacon, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, then uncover and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon. Meanwhile boil 800g small waxy potatoes. Stir 30g butter into the sauce, scatter with parsley and serve with the potatoes.
W: Little Cosette's winter pears with chocolate sauce
Cosette sent out alone into the dark winter woods to fetch the water

Whole pears poached in vanilla, cinnamon and orange syrup, with a warm dark chocolate sauce. Simmer 1 litre of water, 200g caster sugar, 1 tsp vanilla, 1 cinnamon stick and 3 strips of orange peel in a pan that fits the pears snugly. Add 4 peeled firm pears with their stalks on, cover with a circle of baking paper and poach gently for 25 minutes, turning now and then, until tender. Cool in the syrup for 30 minutes. Heat 125ml thickened cream until steaming, pour over 100g chopped dark chocolate and stir until smooth. Serve each pear standing in a little syrup with the warm chocolate sauce poured over.
K: the students making plans by candlelight in the back room of the café

Red wine warmed with honey, orange, cinnamon, clove and star anise, served steaming in glasses. Put 750ml red wine, 250ml water, 80g honey, 1 sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves and 2 star anise in a saucepan and warm over low heat for 12 minutes, stirring until the honey melts. Do not let it boil. Take off the heat and steep for 10 minutes, then ladle into 4 heatproof glasses with a slice of orange in each.

dishes.n: Valjean's loaf with salted butter and radishes
dishes.make_ahead: Bake up to 1 day ahead and keep in a paper bag; refresh at 200C for 5 minutes. Soften the butter and trim the radishes up to 4 hours ahead

ingredients.item: bread flour, plus extra for dusting

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and warm water to a shaggy, sticky dough. No kneading.
Cover and leave to rise until doubled and bubbly.
Tip onto a well floured bench, fold the edges in to make a round and set it seam side down on floured baking paper.
Heat the oven to 240C with a lidded cast iron pot inside while the loaf rests.
Lift the loaf on its paper into the hot pot, slash the top and bake with the lid on, then lid off until dark and crusty.
Cool on a rack, then tear and serve with the butter, radishes and salt flakes.

dishes.make_ahead: Make up to 1 week ahead; keep sealed under its fat in the fridge and bring to room temperature for 30 minutes before serving

ingredients.item: pork belly, skin removed, in 3cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150C. Toss the pork with the salt and pepper in a small lidded casserole with the garlic, bay, thyme and water.
Cover and cook slowly until the meat falls apart and sits in its own fat.
Pick out the herbs, then shred the pork and garlic with two forks, working in enough of the fat to make it soft and spreadable.
Pack into jars or a bowl, pour the rest of the fat over the top and chill until set.
Serve at room temperature with the toasted baguette, cornichons and mustard.

veg.make_ahead: Make up to 3 days ahead and keep covered in the fridge; bring to room temperature for 30 minutes before serving

steps.text: Cook the eschalots and garlic in half the butter until soft.
Add the mushrooms and thyme and cook over high heat until dark and all the liquid has gone.
Cool, then mash in the cream cheese, the rest of the butter and the lemon juice and season well.
Pack into a bowl and chill until firm.
Serve at room temperature with the toasted baguette, cornichons and mustard.

dishes.make_ahead: Make up to 2 days ahead; it is better reheated. Chill in the pot and warm gently, boiling the potatoes on the night

steps.text: Fry the lardons in a large heavy casserole until crisp, then lift out.
Season the chicken and brown it well in the bacon fat in batches, skin side first. Lift out.
Brown the eschalots and mushrooms in the same pot.
Stir in the garlic and flour, then the wine, stock, bay and thyme. Return the chicken and bacon, cover and simmer gently.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Take the lid off and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon.
Stir in the butter, scatter with parsley and serve with the potatoes.

veg.make_ahead: Make up to 2 days ahead and reheat gently; boil the potatoes on the night

ingredients.item: portobello and Swiss brown mushrooms, thickly sliced

steps.text: Brown the big mushrooms hard in the oil in a large heavy casserole in batches, then lift out.
Brown the eschalots and button mushrooms in the same pot.
Stir in the garlic, flour and smoked paprika, then the wine, stock, soy sauce, bay and thyme. Return the browned mushrooms and simmer gently, half covered.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Season, stir in the butter, scatter with parsley and serve with the potatoes.

dishes.n: Little Cosette's winter pears with chocolate sauce
dishes.make_ahead: Poach the pears up to 3 days ahead and keep them in their syrup in the fridge; make the sauce on the night

steps.text: Simmer the water, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and orange peel in a saucepan that fits the pears snugly until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pears, cover with a circle of baking paper and poach gently, turning now and then, until a knife slides in easily.
Cool the pears in the syrup.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth.
Stand each pear in a shallow bowl with a spoonful of syrup and pour over the warm chocolate sauce.

dishes.make_ahead: Warm and steep the wine up to 2 hours ahead, then reheat gently without boiling

steps.text: Put everything in a saucepan and warm over low heat, stirring until the honey melts. Do not let it boil.
Take off the heat and leave to steep.
Ladle into 4 heatproof glasses with a slice of orange in each.

af.make_ahead: Warm and steep up to 2 hours ahead, then reheat gently

steps.text: Put the grape juice, tea, honey, orange and spices in a saucepan and warm over low heat.
Take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and leave to steep.
Ladle into 4 heatproof glasses with a slice of orange in each.
